change: two changes to the consecutive-halt guard in scripts/canary_supervisor.py: the counter is keyed on the failing CALL rather than the cell, and SAME_CELL_MAX is raised from 3 to 8
context: applied with 39 of 941 cells outstanding, so the exposure to a looser guard is bounded by how little work remains.
honest_note_on_the_evidence: the keying correction would NOT have prevented any of the three stops that motivated it. All three were a single call failing consecutively by itself. The correction is right on its own merits and prevents a class of false stop, but the threshold is what actually unblocks this run, and conflating the two would overstate the case for either.
note: Append-only. Grants no new spend authority and changes no cap.

owner_instruction.referring_to: merge the per-call fix and raise the halt limit to 8

residual_risk: a genuinely deterministic failure now burns 8 attempts before stopping instead of 3. At the observed ~$0.009 per abandoned call that is about $0.05 of extra uncertain spend per such failure, against a $4.00 ceiling currently at $0.92.
the_keying_correction: separate from the threshold and independently justified. Determinism is a property of a call, not a cell: one judgment cell issues a checker call, a judge query per slot, and a verdict, each able to fail independently. Pooling their halts tripped the guard on cells whose every call was still succeeding on retry. A single call failing repeatedly still collapses to one key and still stops the run, which is the property worth keeping; a test pins both directions.
the_mismatch_it_fixes: the limit of 3 was calibrated when a hung call cost 600 seconds, so three attempts was already 30-plus minutes of evidence. The 2026-08-01 transport amendment cut the timeout to 120s, which made retries five times cheaper but left the attempt count untouched. A call needing five attempts, which was observed repeatedly, now trips a limit built for far slower retries. Eight attempts at 120s is roughly 16 minutes of wall clock, less than three attempts used to cost.
this_is_a_safety_relaxation: Stated plainly, as amendment 7 was. The consecutive-halt limit is named in the policy artifact as one of the three constraints that bound real risk. Raising it is the owner's call, not an operational one, and it is recorded as a deviation rather than as housekeeping.
what_is_not_changed: the $40.00 stage cap enforced by the client against the chained usage ledger
the enumerated benign-transient signature, which still stops on anything novel
the requirement that the halted cell have no result row
